title: Boats to Save People
hints: the heaviest person always needs a boat - can they ever share it with someone, and if so, who is the best possible boat-mate for them?
if the heaviest person can share a boat with anyone at all, they can share it with the lightest remaining person, since that's the best chance of fitting under the limit
sort everyone by weight, then use two pointers: one at the lightest, one at the heaviest person remaining

if the lightest and heaviest together fit within limit, put them in one boat and advance both pointers; otherwise the heaviest goes alone, advance only that pointer - either way, one boat is used per step

why is pairing the heaviest with the lightest never worse than pairing the heaviest with some middle-weight person? because if the heaviest can't fit with the lightest, it can't fit with anyone, and if it can fit with the lightest, that pairing frees up the more constrained middle-weight people to pair with each other later
commonMistakes: pairing the two heaviest people together instead of heaviest with lightest, which wastes boat capacity and can increase the total boat count
always sending the heaviest person alone without first checking whether they could share with the lightest remaining person
off-by-one errors in the two-pointer loop when exactly one person remains (that person still needs their own boat)

content.problemStatement:
You're given the weight of each person in `people`, and every boat can carry at most 2 people at a time, as long as their combined weight does not exceed `limit`.

**Return the minimum number of boats needed to carry everyone across.**
constraints: each boat carries at most 2 people
notes: every person weighs exactly limit / 2, so all pairs fit
every person weighs exactly limit, so nobody can share a boat
